venue.name: Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, Parliamentary Education Office
venue.description: The Parliament Buildings at 501 Belleville Street are the home of the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, where elected MLAs debate and pass provincial laws. The Parliamentary Education Office and the Tour Office run free guided tours, school programmes and classroom sessions about the building and about how the province is governed. School bookings are made through an online form, and school groups use a separate entrance at the back of the building. There is also a free self guided route with tour books available at the Tour Desk in a variety of languages.

facility_notes.washrooms: If possible, plan to use washrooms prior to your arrival as the public washrooms in the Parliament Buildings are not well suited to large groups. If it is not possible, please let your guide know that you would like a washroom break included as part of the tour.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is no public parking for visitors on the property. Public parking is available on surrounding streets and in nearby lots. Their school entrance map shows a bus drop off location on Belleville Street.

restrictions: Please arrive at the school entrance at the back of the Parliament Buildings 10 minutes before the time of your tour.
Tours may be cancelled at any time due to events on the Legislative Precinct.
Tour times, tour routes and the Parliamentary sitting schedule are subject to change without notice.
venue.hours_notes: Weekdays the Parliament Buildings are open between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm. In the summer season they also open on Saturday and Sunday, with guided tours between 9:00 am and 4:40 pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: From Monday, May 18 to Sunday, August 30 the buildings are open seven days a week for free guided tours. After August 31 they open Monday to Friday only and are closed on weekends and holidays through the fall and winter.

programs.name: School guided tour
programs.description: A free guided tour of the Parliament Buildings for school groups, introducing the role of the Legislative Assembly, the history of the building and the provincial level of government. Allow up to 1 hour, or up to 1.5 hours if you also want to watch a debate. Groups who want to watch a debate must book the Tour with Gallery option and are given 20 minutes in the Public Gallery after the tour. Some rooms are closed and the tour is shortened on days when the Assembly is meeting. They will let your school's MLA know you are coming and invite them to meet the class, although MLAs cannot be guaranteed.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the public rooms of the Parliament Buildings with a guide who explains what happens in each one and how laws are made. Groups who book the gallery option then sit in the Public Gallery for about twenty minutes and watch MLAs debating.
programs.our_note: Take the group to the washroom before you arrive. They say plainly that the public washrooms do not suit large groups. Only book the gallery option after checking their sitting calendar, and be aware that the topics debated are whatever the MLAs are dealing with that day. Groups over 40 have to be split into more than one tour.
programs.practical_summary: Free, up to an hour, and capped at 40 people including the adults. There is no parking on site and no lunch space mentioned, so plan the bus drop off and lunch elsewhere.
programs.cancellation_note: Tours may be cancelled at any time due to events on the Legislative Precinct.
programs.evidence: The maximum size for each tour is 40 people (including all students and accompanying adults).

programs.name: Little Legislators
programs.description: A free school tour aimed at younger, more kinesthetic learners and best suited to students in kindergarten to grade 3. Offered in English or French. It covers identity and family, community participation and Indigenous peoples, and introduces debate, law making and provincial governance. Through a mock debate, children see how a group of people come together to make decisions and how to make their voices heard. Book through the same tour request form and add a comment in the box titled Topic of Interest to say you want Little Legislators. Groups use the school entrance.
programs.what_children_do: Take part in a mock debate inside the Parliament Buildings, standing up and speaking as decisions are made, alongside a walk through the building.
programs.our_note: This is the version to ask for if your group is under about eight. You have to say so in the topic box on the booking form, otherwise you will be given the standard tour. Being offered in French as well is worth knowing if you run a francophone or immersion programme.
programs.practical_summary: Free, aimed at kindergarten to grade three, and booked through the same online form as the standard school tour. How long it runs, the group size limit and how much notice they need are not published, so ask.
programs.evidence: Little Legislators is a free school tour program aimed at younger, more kinesthetic learners, and is best suited to students K-3.

programs.name: Parliamentary Play and Tour for Schools
programs.description: An outdoor costumed play on the grounds followed by a guided tour inside the Parliament Buildings, about 80 minutes in total and free. Teachers choose between two plays. Who's in Charge? is recommended for grades K to 6 and follows a parliament of owls looking at British Columbia's system of government, with a tour focused on participation and representation. The Story of Here is recommended for grades 7 to 12 and looks at how the Parliamentary Precinct has been shaped by Indigenous history, colonialism, democracy and the suffrage movement. Maximum of 35 students and 5 adults, and they normally ask for a minimum of 15 people. Runs Tuesday, May 19, 2026 to Tuesday, June 23, 2026 on weekdays only.
programs.what_children_do: Sit outside on the grounds to watch a short play performed by actors in period costume, then go inside for a guided tour of the building.
programs.our_note: The play half is outdoors, so bring what the weather needs and something to sit on. It runs for about five weeks in late spring only, so it is easy to miss. For summer 2026 the meeting spot is sent out closer to the day rather than published, so watch for that email.
programs.practical_summary: Free, about 80 minutes, capped at 35 students with 5 adults, and they usually want at least 15 people. Two start times a day on weekdays, and the meeting spot is confirmed nearer the date.
programs.evidence: Group Size: Maximum of 35 students and 5 adults.

programs.name: Self guided visit
programs.description: Visitors are welcome to walk the public parts of the Parliament Buildings on their own at any time between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday excluding holidays, all year round. Self guided tour books are available in a variety of languages at the Tour Desk. No booking is needed. On summer weekends, when the buildings are also open, visitors must join a guided tour instead.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the public rooms at their own pace, following a printed tour book picked up at the Tour Desk.
programs.our_note: Useful when you cannot get a tour slot or you want a short stop rather than a whole morning. You still go through security screening at the main entrance, so leave a few extra minutes with a group. A big group turning up unannounced is worth phoning about first.
programs.practical_summary: Free, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm all year, and no booking needed. No group size limit is published for this, and there is no parking on site.
programs.evidence: Visitors are welcome to take their own self-guided tour at any time between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm

programs.name: Virtual Classroom session
programs.description: A live online session hosted by a Parliamentary Tour Guide, with stories and photographs about the Legislative Assembly. Appropriate for students in grades 3 to 12, and they also present to community organisations. You choose either a 30 or a 45 minute session and one of four topics: BC Parliament 101, Levels of Government, How a Bill Becomes a Law, or a session for groups who have applied for a School Travel Grant. Sessions run on Zoom or Teams, with Zoom preferred, and are offered between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm Monday to Thursday. A minimum of 5 people is required. You can ask them to invite your school's MLA to join, which adds about 15 minutes.
programs.what_children_do: Join a live video call from the classroom with a tour guide who shows photographs and tells stories about the Parliament Buildings. In the law making session they watch short clips of a real debate and take part in a mock parliament.
programs.our_note: The obvious choice if the trip to Victoria is not on. Microphones and cameras are preferred but not required, so it works for a class watching on one screen. If you want more than one session, tell them, so they can vary the topic and avoid repeating material.
programs.practical_summary: Thirty or forty five minutes on Zoom or Teams, Monday to Thursday between 9:30 am and 3:00 pm, with at least five people. The price is not published, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: We require a minimum of 5 people to book a session.

programs.name: Speaker in the Schools
programs.description: A 60 minute classroom programme that introduces students to the work of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly with the Honourable Raj Chouhan. After a short introduction to the work of the Legislature, the Speaker takes open questions from the students. Enquiries go to the Parliamentary Education Office by email.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in their own classroom while the Speaker talks about what the Legislature does, then put their own questions to him.
programs.our_note: This one comes to you and depends on one person's diary, so ask well ahead about dates. Have the class prepare questions, because the open question time is the bulk of the hour.
programs.practical_summary: A 60 minute visit to your classroom. The cost, how far they will travel and how much notice they need are not published, so email the education office.
programs.evidence: This 60 minute classroom program introduces students to the work of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly

gaps: Their pages give three different phone numbers for tour enquiries, so the phone number is left blank here and all three are listed in the conflicts note. The school tours page gives 250.387.9243, the Little Legislators page gives 250-387-1771 and the general tour information page gives 250-387-6668. None of the pages is dated.
No price is published for the Virtual Classroom sessions or for Speaker in the Schools, although tours of the building are free.
No youngest age is stated anywhere. Little Legislators is the youngest programme and starts at kindergarten, so nothing is said about preschool or daycare groups.
The standard school tour has no published grade range at all.
How much notice they need for a school booking is not stated. The booking form only shows times still available.
How many adults have to come is not stated. The play caps adults at 5 and the standard tour counts adults in its 40 person total.
Nowhere to eat is mentioned for school groups. There is a Parliamentary Dining Room but it is a restaurant, not a lunch room for classes.

Whether the tour route inside is step free is not stated on the pages we read. Their transportation page says the buildings are reachable by wheelchair or mobility scooter, which is about getting there rather than the route inside, so that field was left blank.
There is no rain plan mentioned for the outdoor half of the Parliamentary Play and Tour.
There is no public parking on the property. Their school entrance map shows a bus drop off on Belleville Street, but no coach parking is described.
Bookings go through Checkfront, an outside booking service, rather than through their own site.

The school entrance map, the chamber photo and the exterior photo were used for images. Two photos on the school tours page had no alt text and two more image tags on that page pointed at an empty file path, so they were skipped.
No coordinates are published on the site, so the address was recorded for geocoding.

conflicts.note: Three of their pages give three different phone numbers for tour enquiries. They are 250 387 9243 on the school tours page, 250 387 1771 on the Little Legislators page and 250 387 6668 on the general tour information page. Email tours@leg.bc.ca is given consistently on all three, so that is the safer first try.
